newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Canada cuts bank rate 25 bps to 4.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank Canada cuts bank rate 25 bps to 4.0 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada cut its key Bank Rate on Wednesday by 25 basis points to 4.0 percent by conducting special purchase and resale operations at 4.0 percent.
The move effectively lowered its target range for the overnight lending rate to 3.50-4.0 percent from 3.75-4.25 percent, money market traders said.
The Bank Rate is the top of the central bank's target range for the overnight rate, at which it lends to financial institutions in its role as lender of last resort.
A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

In a news release after the cut, the Bank said with a growing focus in financial markets on Canada's low inflation, significantly improving public finances and sharp swing into surplus on the country's balance of international payments, the dollar had appreciated and short-term money market interest rates had declined.
The Bank said the rate cut was consistent with this change in the mix of monetary conditions (with a stronger currency and lower short-term interest rates).

The Bank of Canada rate cut prompted moves among the country's chartered banks to lower prime rates to 5.50 percent from 5.75 percent. Canadian T-bills rallied following the rate cut and the Canadian dollar traded steady.

It was the eighth time this year the Bank of Canada has cut short-term interest rates and the seventh time the Bank has cut rates independent of an easing by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Bank has lowered short-term rates by 200 basis points this year and 425 basis points since May, 1995.
